## Big idea in one line

**Advice** = the code that runs at a chosen moment around a method.  
Pick the annotation that matches the moment you need — or use **`@Around`** when you need full control (before + after + decide whether to call the method).

```text
        @Around (outer wrapper)
   ┌────────────┴────────────┐
@Before                   @After / @AfterReturning / @AfterThrowing
   │                           │
   └──────── method body ──────┘
```

***

## Topic 1 — Advice cheat sheet

| Annotation | Runs | Typical use |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `@Before` | Before method | Auth check, log entry args |
| `@AfterReturning` | After success (can see return value) | Log result |
| `@AfterThrowing` | After exception | Log error |
| `@After` | After method finishes (success or fail) | Cleanup-ish logging |
| `@Around` | Wraps the whole call | Timing, retry, modify args/result |

`@After` runs for both success and failure (like `finally` relative to the join point).  
`@AfterReturning` only on success; `@AfterThrowing` only on failure.

***

## Topic 2 — `@Before`

```java
@Before("execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..))")
public void before(JoinPoint jp) {
    System.out.println("BEFORE " + jp.getSignature().getName());
    System.out.println("args=" + Arrays.toString(jp.getArgs()));
}
```

`JoinPoint` gives method signature and arguments.

***

## Topic 3 — `@AfterReturning` / `@AfterThrowing` / `@After`

```java
@AfterReturning(
    pointcut = "execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..))",
    returning = "result")
public void afterReturn(JoinPoint jp, Object result) {
    System.out.println("RETURNED " + result);
}

@AfterThrowing(
    pointcut = "execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..))",
    throwing = "ex")
public void afterThrow(JoinPoint jp, Throwable ex) {
    System.out.println("THREW " + ex.getMessage());
}

@After("execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..))")
public void afterFinally(JoinPoint jp) {
    System.out.println("AFTER (always) " + jp.getSignature().getName());
}
```

Names in `returning = "result"` / `throwing = "ex"` must match the method parameter names.

***

## Topic 4 — `@Around` (most powerful)

```java
@Around("execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..))")
public Object around(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp) throws Throwable {
    long start = System.currentTimeMillis();
    try {
        Object result = pjp.proceed(); // call the real method
        return result;
    } finally {
        long took = System.currentTimeMillis() - start;
        System.out.println(pjp.getSignature().getName() + " took " + took + "ms");
    }
}
```

### Rules that bite beginners

1. **`proceed()`** runs the target method (and later advice further inside).  
2. If you forget `proceed()`, the business method never runs.  
3. You may call `proceed(args)` with modified arguments.  
4. You may change / replace the returned value.  
5. Signature returns `Object` and may declare `throws Throwable`.

```text
@Around
  ├─ code before
  ├─ pjp.proceed()  → real method
  ├─ code after success
  └─ catch / finally as you like
```

***

## Topic 5 — Order when several advice apply

Multiple aspects → use `@Order` on aspect classes.  
Prefer **one clear `@Around` for timing** rather than fighting a pile of overlapping advice while learning.

Rough intuition for a single aspect stack:

```text
@Around start
  @Before
    method
  @AfterReturning / @AfterThrowing
  @After
@Around end
```

(Exact nesting can get subtle with many aspects — start simple.)

## Practice lab (IDE steps)

### Step 1 — Service with success + failure paths

```java
public String ok() { return "OK"; }
public String fail() { throw new IllegalStateException("boom"); }
```

### Step 2 — Add `@Before` and `@After`

Call both methods; confirm AFTER runs even when `fail()` throws (after your exception handler / error path as applicable).

### Step 3 — `@AfterReturning` vs `@AfterThrowing`

Print return value on `ok`; print exception message on `fail`.

### Step 4 — Replace with `@Around` timer

Remove the noisy before/after logs if you want; wrap with `@Around` + `proceed()` + duration log.  
Confirm forgetting `proceed()` breaks the API (then restore it).

***

## Short map to keep

```text
@Before          = entrance
@AfterReturning  = success exit + return value
@AfterThrowing   = failure exit + exception
@After           = finally-like
@Around          = full remote control via proceed()
```

## Exercises

1. Which advice can both measure time and skip the real method?  
2. What method on `ProceedingJoinPoint` invokes the target?  
3. Difference between `@After` and `@AfterReturning`?  
4. Why must `@Around` methods return `Object`?  
5. How do you bind the thrown exception into an `@AfterThrowing` method?
